newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares set high, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares set high, seen extending gains.

text.p: Most Polish shares on Thursday fell but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main index to a 34-month high and analysts said the main, after falling twice this week following a surge, appeared ready to extend gains.

"It seems the change in mood (after the falls) had a healing effect on what started two weeks ago and now there's a chance for more gradual growth in the near term," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
The main market has risen 10.7 percent in February to 17,822.2 points, and analysts saw rises to at least 18,000 this month before a more significant correction hit.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.7 percent to 17,822.2 points and turnover fell 10 percent to 217.7 million ($71.8 million) zlotys on both markets. Losers led gainers by 43 to 35 with 10 stocks flat.

Analysts said the co-ruling Peasant Party's Wednesday decision to sack its agriculture minister might not slow the current bull market, as might not imminent fuel price rises after the finance ministry's Thursday decision to free them.
Analysts said continued rises by large-cap stocks were a good sign, such as top gainer aluminium plant Kety, up by the daily maximum 10 percent, and construction firm Budimex, up by 9.8 percent.

They said construction firm Espebepe, which rose by 9.6 percent, enjoyed one of its occasional speculative surges on retail investors' hopes the firm would clinch a deal with its creditors sometime after the latter meet on March 14.

Mass privatisation NFI units fell 0.9 percent to 163.5 zlotys ($53.9 pct) in regular trade and rose 0.6 percent to 167 zlotys ($55.1) in 22.2-million-zloty (7.3 million) continuous trade, where most stocks rose in 28.4-million-zloty ($9.4 million) trade.
